ei.title: From a Kid to a Champion
ei.subject: 영어1

fullPassage:
My name is Bliksem, which means "lightning." My parents named me this because they wanted me to be faster than anyone else. Born in the Netherlands, a country with more bicycles than people, I learned to ride a bike almost as soon as I could walk. I loved feeling the breeze in my hair. When I was eleven, a junior bicycle race was held in our small town. I entered the race as the youngest rider. Before the race started, I looked around the crowd, and I couldn't believe my eyes! My hero, Gabriel Martinez, the cycling world champion, was standing there! I ran over and asked, "You're Gabriel Martinez, right? Can I have your autograph?" He smiled and said, "If you win, you can." Excited by what he said, I pedaled harder than ever. I came in first and Gabriel was waiting at the finish line. As promised, he handed me his autograph saying, "You outran the others by two laps! You're a real racer, kid!"

Since then, Gabriel has been my mentor. When I turned nineteen, he brought me into his professional team, where only the most skilled and passionate cyclists came together. I felt small and insignificant. I could sprint the fastest on flat courses, but I always fell behind in mountain races. The Netherlands is mostly flat, so I had rarely cycled up steep slopes before. Gabriel was from Bogotá, Colombia, which is high up in the Andes. He had a lot of experience in riding on hills and mountains, so he was always the first to arrive at the top. He would say, "Riding uphill is painful, but the view at the top is fantastic. Never stop pedaling, kid."

Motivated by Gabriel's encouragement, I participated eagerly in all the training courses, especially the uphill ones. Soon after, my efforts finally paid off in one of the mountain courses. As a domestique, who supports the leader and the team during a cycling race, I was riding in front of Gabriel to shield him from the headwind. Our team was far ahead of the others. Everything was going perfectly until I crashed due to a crack in the road. All four of us fell in the crash, and the other teams passed us by. I was just slightly wounded, but Gabriel's injury was more serious. He urged me to continue on his behalf. But there were a couple of more steep slopes ahead, and I doubted we had a chance. Gabriel read my mind and yelled, "Remember the view at the top. Never stop pedaling whatever it takes, kid. Now go!"

Pedaling with all my strength, I finished second in that race, but I felt a sense of guilt for my fellow team members. I should have been more careful. If I had not crashed, Gabriel would have come in first place, and our team would have won. Surprisingly, Gabriel gave me a gentle hug and said, "I knew you could do it. I'm so proud of you!"

For several years, I assisted Gabriel in races as a domestique. As we cycled together, our team's results flourished. When the time came for his retirement, Gabriel asked the members if I could lead the team in his final race. He said he could no longer ride faster than me in the last sprint to the finish line and insisted that I ought to be the team leader. I was deeply touched and felt a burden on my shoulders. I was determined to make him proud.

Gabriel's final race was the Paris-Roubaix, a 250 km race famed for its cobblestone sections. These bumpy roads were a true test of endurance, talent, and mental power for every cyclist. As the race started, I focused on my strategy and my desire to win. However, the rocky and cobblestone track caused a flat tire and I could not continue. Gabriel offered me his bike without hesitation, saying, "I remember your finishing the race two laps ahead of everyone when I first met you. Never stop pedaling, kid. I'll catch up." The rest of the members urged me on and we continued, pushing ourselves to our limits. When there were only 10 km left in the race, Gabriel caught up with us on a new bicycle. He cut in front of me and said, "Save your energy now for the final sprint. We'll help you to the finish line."

Our speed increased as we approached the finish line, and my teammates worked hard to support me. When the finish line came into view, I began my final sprint with a rush of adrenaline, and our rivals were right on my tail, fighting for the same victory. Finally, I crossed the finish line ahead of my competitors by a nose.

The crowd roared tremendously. They focused on me since I was the first to cross the finish line. As I stood on the podium holding the trophy high, I felt like the glory should go to Gabriel. However, when I looked over, I could see the pride in his eyes.

He said, "That trophy is yours, Captain." It was the first time he had not addressed me as "kid." My teammates approached me as tears welled up in my eyes, saying, "We're counting on you, Captain."

questions.passage: My parents ①<u>named</u> me this because they wanted me to be faster than anyone else. Born in the Netherlands, a country with more bicycles than people, I learned to ride a bike almost as soon as I could walk. I loved ②<u>feeling</u> the breeze in my hair. When I was eleven, a junior bicycle race was ③<u>holding</u> in our small town. I ④<u>entered</u> the race as the youngest rider.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: holding → held (수동태)
det.analysis:
✅ ① named: 과거시제. 'My parents named me' — 적절.

✅ ② feeling: 동명사. 'I loved feeling the breeze' — love + V-ing 구문. 적절.

❌ ③ holding: 원문 'a race was held'에서 수동태 held가 맞음. was holding은 능동('개최하고 있었다')으로 의미가 달라짐. ←정답

✅ ④ entered: 과거시제. 'I entered the race' — 적절.
det.tip: 수동태: was held(개최되었다) vs was holding(개최하고 있었다). 경주는 '개최되는' 것이므로 수동태.

questions.passage: When I turned nineteen, he ①<u>brought</u> me into his professional team, where only the most skilled and ②<u>passionate</u> cyclists came together. I felt small and insignificant. I could ③<u>sprint</u> the fastest on ④<u>flatly</u> courses, but I always fell behind in mountain races. The Netherlands is mostly flat, so I had rarely cycled up steep slopes before.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: flatly → flat (형용사)
det.analysis:
✅ ① brought: 과거시제. 'he brought me into' — bring의 과거형. 적절.

✅ ② passionate: 형용사. cyclists를 수식. 적절.

✅ ③ sprint: 동사원형. 조동사 could 뒤. 적절.

❌ ④ flatly: 원문 'flat courses'에서 형용사 flat이 명사 courses를 수식. 부사 flatly는 명사 수식 불가. ←정답
det.tip: 명사 앞에는 형용사: flat courses(O) / flatly courses(X). flatly = 부사(단호하게).

questions.passage:

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: pedaled → pedaling (stop + V-ing)
det.analysis:
❌ ① pedaled: 원문 'Never stop pedaling'에서 stop + V-ing 구문이 맞음. stop pedaled(X) — stop 뒤에 동명사가 와야 '~하는 것을 멈추다'. ←정답

✅ ② crashed: 과거시제 — 적절.

✅ ③ finished: 과거시제 — 적절.

✅ ④ would have won: 가정법 과거완료(If I had not crashed... would have won). 조건절과 결과절 시제 일치. 적절.
det.tip: stop + V-ing = ~하는 것을 멈추다. stop pedaling(O) / stop pedaled(X). 가정법 과거완료: had p.p. → would have p.p.

questions.passage:
He would say, "Riding uphill is ①<u>painful</u>, but the view at the top is ②<u>terrible</u>. Never stop pedaling, kid."

Motivated by Gabriel's ③<u>encouragement</u>, I participated ④<u>eagerly</u> in all the training courses, especially the uphill ones.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 정상에서의 경치가 환상적이지, 끔찍하지 않다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① painful: 고통스러운 — 원문 그대로. 적절.

❌ ② terrible: 끔찍한 — 원문 fantastic(환상적인). 정상에서의 경치를 칭찬하는 맥락에서 terrible은 정반대. ←정답

✅ ③ encouragement: 격려 — 원문 그대로. 적절.

✅ ④ eagerly: 열심히 — 원문 그대로. 적절.
det.tip: fantastic(환상적인) ↔ terrible(끔찍한). Gabriel은 오르막의 고통 뒤에 오는 보상(전망)을 강조.

questions.passage: Gabriel's final race was the Paris-Roubaix, a 250 km race ①<u>famed</u> for its cobblestone sections. These bumpy roads were a true test of ②<u>endurance</u>, talent, and mental power for every cyclist. As the race started, I focused on my ③<u>strategy</u> and my desire to win. However, the rocky and cobblestone track caused a flat tire and I could not continue. Gabriel offered me his bike without ④<u>eagerness</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: Gabriel은 망설임 없이 자전거를 내주었다. eagerness(열의)가 아닌 hesitation(망설임)이 원문.
det.analysis:
✅ ① famed: 유명한 — 원문 그대로. 적절.

✅ ② endurance: 인내력 — 원문 그대로. 적절.

✅ ③ strategy: 전략 — 원문 그대로. 적절.

❌ ④ eagerness: 열의 — 원문 'without hesitation'(망설임 없이). 'without eagerness'(열의 없이)는 문맥 정반대. Gabriel이 자전거를 '열의 없이' 줬다면 비자발적 느낌. ←정답
det.tip: without hesitation(망설임 없이) = 즉시, 주저 없이. without eagerness(열의 없이) = 마지못해 → 의미 반전.

questions.passage: Motivated by Gabriel's encouragement, I participated eagerly in all the training courses, especially the uphill ones. Soon after, my efforts finally __________ in one of the mountain courses. As a domestique, who supports the leader and the team during a cycling race, I was riding in front of Gabriel to shield him from the headwind. Our team was far ahead of the others. Everything was going perfectly until I crashed due to a crack in the road.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 노력이 마침내 성과를 거둔 부분.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ paid off: 원문 'my efforts finally paid off'(노력이 결실을 맺다). 훈련 참여 → 산악 코스에서 성과.
→ 본문: 'I participated eagerly in all the training courses' 후 'Soon after, my efforts finally paid off'.

❌ ① fell behind: '뒤처졌다' — 성과와 반대.
❌ ② ran out: '바닥났다' — 노력이 바닥나는 맥락 아님.
❌ ④ broke down: '고장났다/무너졌다' — 노력의 결실 맥락 아님.
det.tip: pay off = (노력이) 성과를 거두다, 결실을 맺다.

questions.passage: When the time came for his retirement, Gabriel asked the members if I could lead the team in his final race. He said he could no longer ride faster than me in the last sprint to the finish line and insisted that I ought to be the team leader. I was deeply touched and felt a __________ on my shoulders. I was determined to make him proud.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 팀 리더로 지명되어 어깨에 무게감/부담을 느낌.
det.analysis:
✅ ① burden: 원문 'felt a burden on my shoulders' 일치. 팀 리더 역할의 책임감.
→ 본문: 'insisted that I ought to be the team leader. I was deeply touched and felt a burden'.

❌ ② relief: '안도' — 감동과 결심의 맥락에서 부적절.
❌ ③ pride: '자부심' — 뒤에 'determined to make him proud'이므로 아직 자부심보다 부담감.
❌ ④ shame: '수치심' — 'deeply touched'와 모순.
det.tip: burden = 부담, 짐. felt a burden on my shoulders = 어깨에 부담을 느꼈다.

questions.passage: My name is Bliksem, which means "lightning." My parents named me this because they wanted me to be faster than anyone else. Born in the Netherlands, a country with more bicycles than people, I learned to ride a bike almost as soon as I could walk. I loved feeling the breeze in my hair. When I was eleven, a junior bicycle race was held in our small town. I entered the race as the youngest rider.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 전반부 세부 사항.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 일치: 원문 'Born in the Netherlands'에서 Bliksem이 네덜란드에서 태어남 확인.
→ 본문: 'Born in the Netherlands, a country with more bicycles than people'.

❌ ① 산악 코스에서 가장 빨랐다: 원문 'I always fell behind in mountain races'(산악에서 항상 뒤처짐).

❌ ② Gabriel이 Bliksem보다 어렸다: Gabriel은 세계 챔피언이자 멘토이므로 더 나이가 많음.

❌ ④ Gabriel은 네덜란드 출신이다: 원문 'Gabriel was from Bogotá, Colombia'(콜롬비아).
det.tip: Born in the Netherlands = 네덜란드에서 태어남.

questions.passage:
Everything was going perfectly until I crashed due to a crack in the road. All four of us fell in the crash, and the other teams passed us by. I was just slightly wounded, but Gabriel's injury was more serious. He urged me to continue on his behalf.

Pedaling with all my strength, I finished second in that race, but I felt a sense of guilt for my fellow team members.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 충돌 사고 관련 세부 사항.
det.analysis:
❌ ② 일치하지 않음: 원문 'I was just slightly wounded, but Gabriel's injury was more serious'에서 Bliksem은 가볍게 다치고, Gabriel의 부상이 더 심했음. 선지의 'Bliksem의 부상이 Gabriel보다 심했다'는 반대. ←정답

✅ ① 일치: 원문 'All four of us fell in the crash'.

✅ ③ 일치: 원문 'He urged me to continue on his behalf'(대신 계속하라고 독촉).

✅ ④ 일치: 원문 'I finished second in that race'.
det.tip: slightly wounded = 가벼운 부상. more serious = 더 심각한. 비교 관계 주의.

questions.passage:
Gabriel's final race was the Paris-Roubaix, a 250 km race famed for its cobblestone sections. These bumpy roads were a true test of endurance, talent, and mental power for every cyclist. Finally, I crossed the finish line ahead of my competitors by a nose.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 마지막 경주 세부 사항.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 일치: 원문 'I crossed the finish line ahead of my competitors by a nose'.
→ by a nose = 아슬아슬하게, 간발의 차이로.

❌ ① Paris-Roubaix는 100km가 아니라 250km 경주.

❌ ② Gabriel이 아닌 Bliksem이 마지막 경주에서 우승.

❌ ③ 팀원들은 포기하지 않고 'urged me on and we continued'(독려하며 계속함).
det.tip: by a nose = 아슬아슬하게, 간발의 차이로.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 멘토 Gabriel의 반복적 격려를 통해 Bliksem이 kid에서 Captain으로 성장하는 이야기.
det.analysis:
✅ ② the importance of a mentor's encouragement in personal growth
(개인 성장에서 멘토의 격려가 갖는 중요성)
→ 근거: Gabriel이 반복적으로 'Never stop pedaling'이라며 격려하고, Bliksem이 kid에서 Captain으로 성장.

❌ ① the history of professional cycling
(프로 사이클의 역사)
→ 본문: 사이클 역사를 다루지 않음.

❌ ③ the cultural significance of bicycles in the Netherlands
(네덜란드에서 자전거의 문화적 중요성)
→ 본문: 네덜란드는 배경일 뿐 주제가 아님.

❌ ④ the physical challenges of mountain cycling
(산악 사이클의 신체적 도전)
→ 본문: 신체적 어려움은 소재일 뿐 핵심 주제가 아님.
det.tip: From a Kid to a Champion: 멘토 Gabriel의 격려로 성장한 Bliksem의 이야기.

ch: the importance of a mentor's encouragement in personal growth

the physical challenges of mountain cycling

questions.passage: He would say, "Never stop pedaling, kid." Gabriel read my mind and yelled, "Never stop pedaling whatever it takes, kid. Now go!" Gabriel offered me his bike without hesitation, saying, "Never stop pedaling, kid. I'll catch up." He said, "That trophy is yours, Captain." It was the first time he had not addressed me as "kid." questions.stem: 다음 글에서 Gabriel이 반복하는 "Never stop pedaling"이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 'Never stop pedaling'의 함축 의미.
det.analysis:
✅ ② encouragement to never give up regardless of difficulties
(어려움과 관계없이 절대 포기하지 말라는 격려)
→ 근거: 충돌 후, 가파른 경사 앞에서, 타이어 펑크 후 — 모든 위기 순간에 Gabriel이 이 말을 반복. 단순 페달 밟기가 아닌 삶의 격려.

❌ ① advice on improving cycling technique
(사이클 기술 향상에 대한 조언)
→ 본문: 기술적 조언이 아닌 정신적 격려.

❌ ③ a reminder of the importance of physical fitness
(체력의 중요성에 대한 상기)
→ 본문: 체력이 아닌 정신력/끈기의 메시지.

❌ ④ a strategic instruction to increase speed
(속도를 높이라는 전략적 지시)
→ 본문: 전략 지시가 아닌 포기하지 말라는 격려.
det.tip: Never stop pedaling = 절대 포기하지 마라. 세 번의 위기에서 반복 = 일관된 인생 메시지.

ch: encouragement to never give up regardless of difficulties
a reminder of the importance of physical fitness
a strategic instruction to increase speed

questions.passage: Pedaling with all my strength, I finished second in that race, but I felt a sense of guilt for my fellow team members. I should have been more careful. If I had not crashed, Gabriel would have come in first place, and our team would have won. Surprisingly, Gabriel gave me a gentle hug and said, "I knew you could <u>do it</u>. I'm so proud of you!"
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>do it</u>이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 'I knew you could do it'에서 do it은 위기를 극복하고 경주를 훌륭히 마무리한 것.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 역경을 극복하고 경주에서 좋은 성적을 낸 것
→ 근거: 충돌 후 Bliksem이 혼자 2위로 들어옴. Gabriel은 '해낼 줄 알았다'며 자랑스러워함. 우승이 아닌 '역경 속에서 해내는 것' 자체를 의미.

❌ ② 사이클 타는 기술을 배운 것
→ 본문: 이미 11살 때부터 실력이 있었으므로 '기술 습득'이 아님.

❌ ③ 팀 리더 자리를 차지한 것
→ 본문: 팀 리더 지명은 이보다 나중 이야기.

❌ ④ Gabriel의 사인을 받은 것
→ 본문: 사인은 11살 때 에피소드.
det.tip: do it = 해내다. 충돌에도 불구하고 경주를 잘 마무리한 것에 대한 칭찬.

ch: 역경을 극복하고 경주에서 좋은 성적을 낸 것

Finally, I crossed the finish line ahead of my competitors by a nose.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>They</u>가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 'They focused on me since I was the first'에서 They = 관중들.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 관중들
→ 바로 앞 문장 'The crowd roared tremendously'에서 They = the crowd. 관중이 환호한 후 1등으로 들어온 Bliksem에게 주목.

❌ ② 경쟁 팀 선수들
→ 경쟁자(rivals/competitors)가 아닌 crowd가 선행사.

❌ ③ 경기 운영진
→ 운영진 언급 없음.

❌ ④ Bliksem의 팀 동료들
→ teammates는 별도 문맥. They = crowd.
det.tip: They = 앞 문장의 the crowd(관중들). 대명사의 선행사 찾기.

questions.passage: The rest of the members urged me on and we continued, pushing ourselves to our limits. When there were only 10 km left in the race, Gabriel caught up with us on a new bicycle. He cut in front of me and said, "Save your energy now for the final sprint. <u>We</u>'ll help you to the finish line."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>We</u>가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 'We'll help you to the finish line'에서 We = Gabriel을 포함한 팀 동료들.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ Gabriel을 포함한 팀 동료들
→ He(Gabriel)가 Bliksem에게 말하는 상황. 'We'는 Gabriel 자신 + 다른 팀원들(the rest of the members). Bliksem을 결승선까지 도와주겠다는 의미.

❌ ① 관중들
→ 관중이 선수를 결승선까지 도와줄 수 없음.

❌ ② 경쟁 팀의 선수들
→ 경쟁 상대가 Bliksem을 도와줄 이유 없음.

❌ ④ 경기 주최측
→ 주최측 언급 없음.
det.tip: We = Gabriel + 팀 동료들. 문맥상 Bliksem을 '너(you)'로 부르며, 나머지가 '우리(We)'로 도와주겠다고 함.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오. (6단어) (영어로)
"1등을 했을 것이다."
[조건] (1) would, have, come, in, first, place를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 6단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 내가 충돌하지 않았다면 Gabriel이 1등을 했을 것이다 (가정법 과거완료).
det.analysis:
If I had not crashed, Gabriel __________.

• would have come in first place: 가정법 과거완료 결과절.
  - would have + p.p. = ~했을 것이다.
  - come in first place = 1등으로 들어오다.
• 주어 Gabriel은 빈칸 앞에 이미 있으므로 빈칸에는 술어만.
det.tip: 가정법 과거완료: If + S + had p.p., S + would have p.p. come in first place = 1위를 하다.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오. (6단어) (영어로)

det.korean: Gabriel이 망설임 없이 자신의 자전거를 내주었다.
det.analysis:
Gabriel __________.

• offer + IO(me) + DO(his bike): '~에게 ~를 제공하다' (4형식).

• without hesitation: '망설임 없이' 전치사구.
  - without = ~없이 + hesitation = 망설임.
det.tip: offer + 간접목적어 + 직접목적어: offered me his bike. without hesitation = 망설임 없이.
